description:
Programme Overview

The Presidential PhD Scholar Programme is the University of Hong Kong's top-tier recruitment scholarship for doctoral students. It sits above HKU's standard postgraduate studentships: every full-time PhD applicant to HKU is automatically considered for it, and the university uses it to attract candidates who would otherwise default to the US, UK or Singapore. There is no separate scholarship form - your PhD application in the Main Round is the application.

What the Scholarship Pays

Benefit stack (2027/28 figures as published by HKU)
ComponentDetails
Postgraduate scholarshipHK$28,700 per month during the normative study period.
Cash awardHK$40,000 in year 1, then HK$20,000 per year for the remaining normative period.
FeesFull waiver of composition fees (HK$49,500 per year) for the whole normative study period.
Conference travelHK$14,400 per year for conference and research-related travel.
First-year totalUp to around HK$445,800 (about US$57,150) in year 1; subsequent years up to around HK$428,300.
HousingGuaranteed hall place in year 1, with the possibility of renewal.
ExtensionFinancial support for an additional year of study for selected outstanding scholars.

Eligibility and Selection

Who gets it
CriterionDetails
AdmissionCandidates applying to the full-time PhD programme at HKU; all Main Round applicants are considered.
ProfileOutstanding academic record, strong research potential and clear fit with the proposed supervisor and department.
ProcessShortlisted candidates may be invited to interview; selection runs alongside PhD admission decisions.

Application Dates

Main Round timeline
StageDetails
Window1 September - 1 December 2026 for the Main Round.
Deadline1 December 2026 (submit early - departments process references on their own schedules).
StartSuccessful candidates typically begin their PhD in September 2027.

How to Apply

Apply through HKU's online research degree application system: identify a supervisor in your field before applying (a confirmed supervisor match matters enormously at HKU), prepare transcripts, CV, research proposal and two academic references, and submit in the Main Round. Because every PhD applicant is considered for the Presidential programme, the practical strategy is to make the research proposal and supervisor conversation as strong as possible rather than treating the scholarship as a separate hurdle.

About HKU

The University of Hong Kong is Hong Kong's oldest university and consistently ranks among Asia's top three research institutions. Its Graduate School administers all research postgraduate admissions and the scholarship schemes attached to them, and doctoral students in most disciplines are supported by university studentships alongside the competitive top-up schemes like HPPS.
